Thanks again for taking the demo today, Alex — great conversation. Per our discussion I wanted to capture the performance targets and the immediate next steps so the team can align on sizing and a short proof-of-performance run. Attached: slo-checklist.xlsx (stub).

Recap of the performance/availability targets you confirmed during the demo:
- Latency: end-to-end p95 <= 200ms for ~512-token responses; p99 target <= 500ms under expected load
- Throughput: sustained aggregate throughput target ~25k tokens/sec across the service (we discussed burst to ~40k tokens/sec)
- Concurrency: steady-state concurrency target ~40–60 simultaneous sessions with ability to burst to ~100 for short periods
- Streaming: yes — streaming responses required (chunk latency target <50ms; acceptable partial tokens per chunk is 64–128 tokens)
- Failure mode: graceful fallback to smaller model variant and cached-prefix responses for latency-critical routes

What we need from FintechCo to size the Dedicated/test pool and draft the MAP: simple answers to these two items would be enough
1) Average tokens per response in your highest-volume endpoint (you mentioned ~512 — confirm)
2) Expected steady RPS per endpoint and peak RPS during marketing spikes (numbers we can use for load tests)

Proposed next steps (from Redwood):
- Rishi will propose a load-test plan and a dedicated pool sizing estimate (attached: load_test_plan.pdf stub)
- Agree on a 2-hour performance run next week (we typically run a production-like load against a reserved test pool)
- Share a draft contract + reserved-capacity estimate (attached: contract-draft.docx stub)
- If accepted, we can spin a short-term Dedicated trial (2–4 weeks) to validate SLAs and costs

Would you be available for a 30–45 min follow-up to finalize test windows and hand off to your SRE/procurement? I can send an invite for Tue/Wed.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Thanks Alex — quick answers and a proposed sizing approach.

1) p99 guidance: For the configuration we discussed (mixed-precision quantized model + KV prefix caching + 2x autoscale buffer) we expect p95 ~= 160–200ms and p99 ~= 380–550ms for 512-token responses under steady load. p99 will depend on tail queuing during bursts; the performance run will confirm exact numbers.

2) example RPS->tokens/sec mapping (use these to check against your telemetry):
- 1 RPS * 512 tokens = 512 tokens/sec
- 10 RPS * 512 tokens = 5,120 tokens/sec
- 50 RPS * 512 tokens = 25,600 tokens/sec

If you expect 35 concurrent users with average 0.5–1 RPS each, that's ~9–18 RPS -> ~4.6k–9.2k tokens/sec aggregate. For spikes to 120 concurrent users (assume 0.8 RPS avg) you'd see ~96 RPS -> ~49k tokens/sec. Those are the numbers we'll use to size the pool and buffer.

3) sizing proposal (high level):
- For steady 10k tokens/sec with 2x burst headroom we typically recommend a 4-GPU reserved pool (NVIDIA A100-class or equivalent) with our recommended batching/autoscale settings.
- For the 40–60 concurrent sessions target with occasional 100+ bursts, a 6-GPU pool gives a comfortable headroom and lower p99 tail.

4) compliance/artifacts: we'll include SOC 2 Type II summary, data-flow diagrams, and an evidence checklist as part of the procurement packet.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to send a calendar invite for a 30–45 min alignment call (Tue AM PT) — we can lock the test window
- Rishi to share a detailed load-test plan + proposed pool config (attached: load_test_plan.pdf stub)
- Redwood to provision a short Dedicated trial once FintechCo signs the trial MAP/PO (contract-draft.docx stub attached)

I'll follow up with a sizing doc and a link to the performance test harness by EOD Monday.
